Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G2767; undiluted:--without mixture.
BiblicalUsage: Once, in the most terrible verse in Revelation: whoever worships the beast shall drink of the wine of the wrath of God, which is poured out without mixture into the cup of his indignation. The word is undiluted — wine with no water in it, wrath with nothing to soften it.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for undiluted carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the cup in Revelation, wrath with nothing to soften it, and the urgency of the One who drank it for us.
RelatedTopics: Judgment; God's wrath and refuge; Second Coming
